name: HyperTile
plain: Splits self-attention query tokens into a grid of tiles to cut attention cost at high resolution. At the default swap_size of 2 the grid is fixed, because the last candidate can never be drawn; it only varies per call with swap_size 3 or more and enough divisors. Only the query is rearranged by this patch; keys and values are passed back untouched.
math:
For token count n in {H·W/4^i, i=0..max_depth}: h=round√(n·ar), w=round√(n/ar), ar=W/H.
nh = random divisor pick: candidates d of h with d ≥ max(32,tile_size)//8·f; n = h//d, first swap_size candidates, idx=randint(0,len−1) with exclusive high so the last is never picked; same for nw. f=2^i if scale_depth else 1.
If nh·nw>1: q is rearranged into batch b·nh·nw of (h/nh · w/nw) tokens; output patch rearranges back. RNG is torch.randint so it follows the torch seed state.

props.architectures: UNet-style models where attn1 tokens relate to original_shape by a 4^i factor; applies only on token counts that match exactly.

label: from code
surprise: k and v stay at whole-image layout while q is tiled into a larger batch; the backend then views k and v into that batch by raster order (inference from reading attention.py:1096-1123 and _reshape_qkv_to_heads), so keys need not match the query's tile.

audit.note: nodes_hypertile.py:18-19: randint(low=0, high=len(ns)-1) has an exclusive high, so the last candidate is never picked. At the default swap_size=2 (line 34) high=1, idx is always 0 and the grid is not random. It varies only with swap_size≥3 and at least 3 divisors.
